newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK prisons should be monitored - UK inspector.
newsitem.headline: HK prisons should be monitored - UK inspector.

text.p: Britain's former chief prison inspector called on Friday for an independent inspectorate to monitor Hong Kong prisons after a tour of penal institutions highlighted overcrowding and staffing shortages.

"We would like something like we have in the United Kingdom, which is an independent inspectorate at prisons, preferably led by a judge or retired judge, somebody outside the correctional system who's independent and has sufficient standing to monitor authority," Sir Stephen Tumim told Hong Kong radio.
Hong Kong is a British colony until midnight on June 30, when Britain hands it back to China.
Human rights groups have expressed concern about the future of justice and the already overstretched penal system. They have also condemned overcrowding in prisons.

Tumim, helping to compile the territory's first independent report on its prisons, made the call after visiting 12 facilities, including the High Island detention camp for Vietnamese boatpeople who are classed as illegal immigrants.
Responding to Tumim's call, the government acknowleged in a statement that there was no room for complacency.
"Their views and recommendations will be considered carefully and followed up where appropriate," it said.
Hong Kong's prisons are designed to hold 10,400 inmates, but the current prison population is 12,600.

Tumim highlighted poor hygiene and accommodation at High Island, which he said would be unacceptable in Britain, but he found conditions in regular prisons cleaner and more orderly than some in Britain.
Tumim's study, conducted jointly with human rights groups, has been discussed with Governor Chris Patten, who the groups say supports a more open penal system.
